Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

fail verb

give out, run short; let someone down

also give out, run out, run short, let down, let someone down, words fail me

classical

Caes. BG 7.50 (Lewis & Short): quem jam sanguis vīrēsque dēficiunt
Hor. Epist. 1.11.30: animus sī tē nōn dēficit aequus
Traupman 342, 373

dēficiō, dēficere, dēfēcī, dēfectum

verb, third conjugation (-iō); intransitive, or with an accusative of the person failed

fail, give out, run short

Of strength, voice, light, money, supplies: vīrēs mē dēficiunt, my strength is failing. Traupman uses it for running low: argentum mihi … paululum dēficit (p. 91).

Other words

  • dēsum, deesse, dēfuī — be lacking; let (someone) down

    verb, irregular (sum); with the dative · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 1.9.17 (Lewis & Short): ut neque amīcīs neque etiam aliēniōribus operā, cōnsiliō, labōre dēsim; Traupman 102: alicuī deesse, to let someone down; Traupman p. 102: alicui deesse, let someone down

    Words fail me: mihi verba dēsunt (Traupman 111, 408).

Examples

  • nōn nātūram dēfēcisse sed cūram

    It was not nature that failed, but care.Quint. 1.1.2

  • Numquam ubi diū fuit ignis, dēfēcit vapor.

    Where there has long been a fire, the warmth never fails.Publ. N 31

  • quod petis, hīc est, est Ulubrīs, animus sī tē nōn dēficit aequus

    What you are looking for is here, it is at Ulubrae, if a level mind does not fail you.Hor. Epist. 1.11.29–30

See also fail, tired.
